(iii) At a suitable video teleconferencing facility convenient for the parents of the child involved in the hearing and for the duration of the hearing.
(15) Witnesses and customary evidence. (i) At least 5 days prior to a hearing, the parties shall exchange lists of all documents and materials that each party intends to use at the hearing, including all evaluations and reports. Each party also shall disclose the names of all witnesses it intends to call at a hearing along with a proffer of the anticipated testimony of each witness.
(ii) At least 10 days prior to a hearing, each party shall report the name, title, description of professional qualifications, and summary of proposed testimony of any expert witness it intends to call at the hearing.
(iii) Failure to disclose documents, materials, or witnesses may result in the hearing officer barring their introduction at the hearing.
(iv) Parties must limit evidence to the issues pleaded, except by order of the hearing officer or with the consent of the parties.
(v) The rules of evidence shall be relaxed to permit the development of a full evidentiary record. 28 U.S.C. appendix, servicing as guide.
(vi) All witnesses testifying at the hearing shall be advised by the hearing officer that making any false statement with intent to commit a crime to knowingly make a false, materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement to a representation to a department or agency of the U.S. Government as to any matter within the jurisdiction of that department or agency, and may result in a fine or imprisonment.
(vii) A party calling a witness shall bear the witness' travel and expenses associated with testifying at the hearing. The DoDEA school or the Military Department concerned shall pay such expenses if a witness is called by the hearing officer.
(viii) The parties shall have the right to cross-examine witnesses testifying at the hearing.

(ix) The hearing officer may issue an order compelling a party to make a subpoena for witnesses employed by, or under control of, the party available for testimony at the party's expense or to submit specific documentary or physical evidence for inspection by the hearing officer or for submission into the record on motion of either party or on the hearing officer's own motion.
(x) When the hearing officer determines that a party has failed to obey an order to make a subpoena with witnesses available for testimony or to submit specific documentary or physical evidence, in accordance with the hearing officer's order, and that such failure is in knowing and willful disregard of the order, the hearing officer shall issue as part of a written report on the matter and may order appropriate sanctions.
(14) Transcripts. (i) A verbatim transcript of any deposition taken by a party shall be provided to the opposing party in hardcopy format or as attached to an electronic email with prior permission of the recipient. If a Military Department or Command takes a deposition, the verbatim transcript of that deposition shall be provided to the parent(s) in hardcopy.
(ii) A verbatim written transcript of the due process hearing shall be arranged by the hearing officer and shall be made available to the parties in hardcopy format or as an attachment to an electronic email, with prior permission of the recipient, on demand and without cost to the parent(s), and a copy of the verbatim written transcript of the hearing shall become a permanent part of the record.
(15) Hearing officer's decision. (i) The hearing officer shall make written findings of fact and conclusions of law and shall set forth both in the written decision addressing the issues presented in the due process complaint, the resolution of those issues, and the rationale for the resolution.
(ii) The hearing officer's decision on the case shall be based on the record, which shall include the petition, the verbatim transcript of the hearing, exhibits admitted into the record, pleadings or correspondence properly filed and served on all parties, and such
